# The sea, two objects: SeaNear, a 34 m disc of 1 m cells around the headland, and SeaFar, a ring from
# 15 to 90 m of 4 m cells (baked with a coarse spacing: the fog dissolves it and it reaches the horizon).
# Every vertex is jittered in height, so each facet catches the moon at its own angle: white dither
# glints on a dark sea. Up Z, sea level z 0.
new
add mesh grid --name SeaNear --size 1 --x-subdivisions 34 --y-subdivisions 34 --location 0 0 0
scale 34 34 1
apply --scale
material new Sea --base-color 0.133 0.137 0.137
mode edit
select vert where "pos.x * pos.x + pos.y * pos.y > 289"
delete vert
select all
randomize --amount 0.18 --seed 21
mode object
add mesh grid --name SeaFar --size 1 --x-subdivisions 45 --y-subdivisions 45 --location 0 0 -0.05
scale 180 180 1
apply --scale
material new SeaFar --base-color 0.133 0.137 0.137
mode edit
select vert where "pos.x * pos.x + pos.y * pos.y < 225 || pos.x * pos.x + pos.y * pos.y > 8100"
delete vert
select all
randomize --amount 0.5 --seed 22
mode object
shade flat
export sea.glb
